title: 3989. Maximum Consistent Columns in a Grid

examples.explanation: Remove column 2 and keep columns 0 and 1, which gives |grid[0][1] − grid[0][0]| = |0 − (−2)| = 2 <= limit. Thus, the maximum number of columns that can remain is 2.

Remove column 1 and keep columns 0 and 2, which gives |grid[0][2] − grid[0][0]| = |1 − 1| = 0 <= limit and |grid[1][2] − grid[1][0]| = |2 − 2| = 0 <= limit. Thus, the maximum number of columns that can remain is 2.
Remove either column 0 or column 1, since |grid[0][1] − grid[0][0]| = |5 − (−5)| = 10 > limit. Thus, the maximum number of columns that can remain is 1.

hints: Think of each column as one item in a subsequence. Two columns a and b with a < b can be adjacent in the remaining grid only if |grid[i][b] - grid[i][a]| <= limit for every row i.
Precompute whether every pair of columns (a, b) is compatible.
Let dp[j] be the maximum number of columns in a valid remaining grid whose last column is j.
For each j, try all previous columns i < j. If columns i and j are compatible, update dp[j] = max(dp[j], dp[i] + 1).
The answer is the maximum value of dp[j].
